newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX ELECTRICITY CALLED HIGHER AFTER FRIDAY RISE.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX ELECTRICITY CALLED HIGHER AFTER FRIDAY RISE.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were called to open flat to higher Monday after finishing higher Friday on shortcovering and unplanned outage of a unit at the Four Corners power plant in New Mexico.

In over-the-counter business, September Palo Verde (PV) futures were quoted at $31.75-32.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) against Friday's settlement at $31.77, and September California-Oregon Border (COB) was talked at $23.00-23.50 versus Friday's close of $23.40.
Day-ahead firm peak prices in the West were generally firmer, quoted at $42.00-44.00 at PV and $21.00-22.50 at COB.
Brokers and traders said the early cash market was buoyed by forecasts of dry and very warm weather in parts of the Pacific Northwest.
Forecasters called for the Northwest to run two to six degrees F above normal with well below normal precipitation.
Temperatures in western section of the Southwest would remain three to six degrees F above normal and the east section as much as five degrees below normal.
On the upside, analysts assessed chart resistance for September PV at $32.40 and September COB at 24.20-24.50.
Market sources said level of activity would return to normal today after many players were away late last week to attend an industry conference in Vancouver, B.C.
The 750 megawatt (MW) unit 5 at the Four Corners plant in New Mexico was shut last Thursday for repairs and expected to resume operation Saturday.
The 1,221 MW Palo Verde nuclear power unit 2 in Arizona slipped to 86 percent of generating capacity as the unit coasts down to a scheduled refueling outage September 6.
